title: API 570 Training in St. Louis: Piping Inspector Exam Prep
description: API 570 exam prep online for St. Louis and Metro East piping inspectors: Wood River unit piping, Hartford transfer lines, CUI, injection points, B31.3.
h1: API 570 training in St. Louis: self-paced exam preparation for refinery, transfer and terminal piping inspectors from Roxana to Hartford and Sauget
html:
API 570 exam prep for process piping inspectors in the St. Louis region

Pipe is what holds the St. Louis area's oil and chemical industry together. Inside the Wood River refinery at Roxana, unit piping moves crude, gas oil, hydrogen, amine and sour water between columns, heaters and reactors. Beyond the refinery fence, transfer lines and manifolds connect the refinery and the pipelines arriving at Wood River and Hartford to tank farms and truck racks, and further east lies Patoka, the crude hub that Enbridge plans to link to Wood River with a new line. The Sauget chemical plants south of East St. Louis run process piping of their own. Each of these systems needs people who can split piping into circuits, place and read CMLs, calculate corrosion rates and remaining life, and judge whether a repaired line can go back into service. That is the scope of the API 570 Piping Inspector certification.

Atlantis NDT prepares candidates for the API 570 examination with a self-paced online course; an instructor answers the questions you send as you work through it. There is no Atlantis classroom in St. Louis. The portal is where the course lives, and Atlantis's offices are in Houston and Hyderabad. The American Petroleum Institute sets eligibility, administers the API 570 examination at Prometric test centres and issues the piping inspector certification.

Unit piping on a refinery that cokes, cracks and hydrocracks

EIA's 2026 Refinery Capacity Report gives Wood River 77,190 barrels per stream day of delayed coking, 103,000 of catalytic cracking fresh feed and 63,770 of distillate hydrocracking, with production capacity for 168 million cubic feet a day of hydrogen, 1,063 short tons a day of sulfur and 26,000 barrels per stream day of asphalt and road oil. Translated into piping, that means hot gas oil running to the cat cracker, coker heater and fractionator lines carrying heavy residue, high-pressure hydrogen and reactor effluent circuits on the hydrocracker, lean and rich amine lines, sour water headed for the stripper, and traced asphalt rundown and loading lines. Each behaves differently, which is why API 570 asks for piping to be grouped into circuits of similar service and inspected as such rather than treated as one long pipe.

Wood River has been wholly Phillips 66's since the company completed buying Cenovus's half of WRB Refining in October 2025, according to Phillips 66's quarterly results. EIA's report, compiled from January 2026 data, still shows the 50/50 partnership. For an inspector the ownership history matters mainly because piping programmes, CML numbering and record systems can change when owners do.

Off the plot: transfer lines, terminal manifolds and the pipeline boundary

In Hartford, where several pipelines meet storage, Kinder Morgan's Wood River Terminal at 1000 BP Lane in Hartford handles petroleum and ethanol, offers truck loading and unloading, and lists Marathon, Explorer and Phillips 66 as receiving pipelines on its terminal sheet. Explorer Pipeline's shipper manual, in its December 2024 revision, describes Wood River as a mainline pump site with a receiving tank farm. Marathon Pipe Line runs a pipeline from Wood River to Patoka, which MPLX announced in 2017 it would expand. In November 2025 Enbridge said its planned Southern Illinois Connector, a 56-mile line from Wood River to Patoka, is expected to enter service in 2028.

Pipe at these sites changes hands between rulebooks. Hazardous liquid pipelines and their facilities are regulated by PHMSA under 49 CFR Part 195, and the operator's own documents fix where the pipeline integrity programme stops and a facility piping programme built on API 570 begins. Candidates who work around terminals should learn which equipment belongs to which programme before assuming the examination's rules govern a given manifold.

The damage mechanisms on the February and June 2027 API 570 exams

The Publications Effectivity Sheet for the February 2027 and June 2027 windows names API RP 571's third edition and restricts questions to its definitions and fifteen mechanisms. The table pairs each with places a St. Louis piping inspector is likely to meet it.

RP 571 mechanism on the 2027 listTypical circuits in the St. Louis region
3.61 SulfidationHot gas oil, vacuum residue and coker lines, especially carbon steel components that slipped into high-temperature service
3.37 Hydrochloric acid corrosionCrude column overhead lines and the first condensing points downstream
3.58 Sour water corrosion (acidic) and 3.3 amine stress corrosion crackingSour water stripper feed, sulfur recovery unit lines, and amine lines in carbon steel that was not stress relieved
3.22 Corrosion under insulationTraced asphalt, heavy oil and gas oil lines, and insulated lines that cycle or sit idle
3.27 Erosion and erosion-corrosionCoker and slurry service, and elbows or tees downstream of control valves and pumps
3.43 Mechanical fatigue, including vibration-induced fatigueSmall-bore connections near pumps and compressors
3.57 Soil corrosion and 3.45 microbiologically influenced corrosionBuried transfer lines, firewater systems and lines left with stagnant water
Also listed: 3.8, 3.9, 3.14, 3.15, 3.17 and 3.31Atmospheric, boiler water and condensate, caustic, caustic cracking, chloride cracking of austenitic stainless steel and galvanic corrosion

What is missing matters as much. Naphthenic acid corrosion, wet H2S damage, high-temperature hydrogen attack and high-temperature H2/H2S corrosion are on the API 510 list for its current windows but not on the API 570 list for these. A candidate from a heavy-crude refinery may know naphthenic acid corrosion well from the job and find no exam question on it, while losing marks on soil corrosion or vibration fatigue that seemed too ordinary to revise.

CUI on traced asphalt and heavy-oil lines

Asphalt, heavy fuel and gas oil lines are commonly traced with steam or electricity and insulated so that the product keeps moving. RP 571 paragraph 3.22 gives the operating temperature range in which corrosion under insulation is most active; read that range in the current text instead of carrying someone else's rule of thumb into the exam. A line that normally runs hot can spend long periods inside the range when it sits idle, during start-up or when tracing fails, and leaking steam tracing keeps insulation wet. The Mississippi Valley climate adds rain, humid summers and winters that freeze and thaw, all of which open jacketing seams and the gaps around supports and branch connections.

API 570 and API RP 574 set out where CUI inspection should concentrate on a susceptible circuit and how follow-up examination is planned. Learn those provisions from the edition on your effectivity sheet. They are tested as written, and a plant's local practice may be stricter or simply different.

Injection points, mixing points and dead legs

API 570 lets injection points be set up as inspection circuits of their own, because chemicals added to a process stream often corrode the pipe downstream of where they enter. On a refinery, the usual examples are neutraliser and corrosion inhibitor injection in a crude column overhead and wash water injection in hydroprocessing effluent systems. API 570 and RP 574 describe how far an injection point circuit extends upstream and downstream and where its thickness monitoring locations belong. Learn the definitions and the inspection recommendations from the current text, because exam questions turn on the exact words.

Dead legs are the other local favourite. Spare pump connections, bypasses, drains, sample points and lines left in place after a unit change hold stagnant fluid, and in a St. Louis winter any of them that hold water can freeze and split as well as corrode. The code expects dead legs to be identified and inspected for the internal damage they attract, with removal considered where a leg serves no purpose. Mixing points, where streams at different temperatures or compositions combine, round out the list of locations that deserve more attention than the circuit average.

Worked example: a hydrotest after repairing a hot gas oil line

The Body of Knowledge expects candidates to calculate a hydrostatic leak test pressure under ASME B31.3, 345.4, and to find the system test limit for a flange in B16.5. Combine the two on a repair. A gas oil line designed for 300 psig at 700°F has a section replaced and will be hydrotested at ambient temperature. The problem gives the pipe's allowable stress as 16,500 psi at 700°F and 20,000 psi at the test temperature, and the line has Class 300 flanges in material group 1.1.

  1. Stress ratio: 20,000 ÷ 16,500 = 1.212, under the cap of 6.5 that 345.4.2 places on it.
  2. Minimum test pressure: 1.5 × 300 × 20,000 ÷ 16,500 = 545.5 psig. Leaving out the temperature correction gives 450 psig, the answer careless candidates pick.
  3. Flange limit: B16.5 allows a system hydrostatic test of up to 1.5 times the 100°F rating, rounded up to the next 25 psi. The Class 300, group 1.1 rating at 100°F is 740 psig, so 1.5 × 740 = 1,110, rounded to 1,125 psig. The test at 545.5 psig is well inside it.
  4. Yield check: B31.3 lets the test pressure be reduced to the maximum that does not exceed yield at test temperature if the calculated figure would stress the pipe beyond it. With these numbers it does not, but the rule itself is fair game.

The same problem appears in many costumes: a pneumatic test with its own lower multiplier, a line whose design temperature is below the test temperature, or a flange of a different group. Practise reading the question for which of those it is before reaching for a formula.

From operator, welder or UT technician to API 570 eligibility

API combines education with experience gained in the last ten years while employed by or under contract to an authorized inspection agency, and it verifies the experience you declare. Around St. Louis, candidates tend to arrive from four directions:

  • UT thickness technicians who read CMLs for contractors on refinery and terminal piping. That is inspection performance as API describes it when it is part of an inspection programme; ASNT SNT-TC-1A NDT training in the area is on the St. Louis NDT training page.
  • Pipe welders and fitters, whose fabrication and repair time counts on the two-year, high-school and no-formal-education routes alongside at least one year of inspection. Many also look at AWS CWI exam prep in St. Louis.
  • Operators moving into inspection, including people who trained in process operations at Lewis and Clark Community College; their operating years help, but the inspection year has to be built.
  • Engineers from SIUE, Missouri S&T and other programmes, who need one year of supervising or performing piping inspection.

The routes and the documents API asks for are on the API 570 certification page.

Fitting B31.3 and API 570 around St. Louis shift work

B31.3 is long, and the open-book half of the exam rewards knowing where things are in it rather than reading it cover to cover. Because the course is self-paced, a sensible order is to learn API 570's closed-book rules for rates, remaining life and intervals by piping class first, then work outwards into B31.3's pressure design, quality factors, blanks, leak tests, impact testing and preheat, and finish with B16.5 ratings. During a turnaround, stop and keep a list of questions from the job; send them to the instructor when you are back on days. Timed practice papers in the closing weeks show whether you can find a table fast enough.

The day itself is 170 questions, 110 closed-book and 60 open-book, with the code PDFs on the screen for the open-book part and nothing brought into the room. Prometric lists test centres in and around St. Louis. Windows and application deadlines are on the API exam schedule page, and the course overview, with its calculation walk-throughs, is on the API 570 training page.

Sponsoring a piping inspection group from a St. Louis site

Refinery inspection departments, terminal operators and contractors around Hartford and Roxana regularly need more than one API 570 inspector. You can enquire for a whole group, with fees quoted on request; API still assesses and examines each person on their own. In the US, Atlantis performs UT, MT, PT and VT inspection, with St. Louis details on the piping inspection page, and does not perform radiography.

faq.q: Can I prepare for API 570 in St. Louis without attending a class?
faq.a: Yes. There is no Atlantis classroom in St. Louis, and none is needed: the API 570 course is online and self-paced, so you start when you enrol and study around your shifts, with an instructor answering your questions. The only fixed point is the examination, which you sit in person at a Prometric test centre within the window API has accepted you for.

faq.q: Is naphthenic acid corrosion on the API 570 exam?
faq.a: Not for the February 2027 and June 2027 windows. Their effectivity sheet limits RP 571 questions to fifteen mechanisms, including sulfidation, hydrochloric acid corrosion, sour water corrosion, corrosion under insulation, soil corrosion and vibration-induced fatigue, and naphthenic acid corrosion is not among them. It is on the API 510 list for that exam's current windows. API changes these lists, so check the sheet for the window you actually book.

faq.q: Are the lines between the refinery and the Hartford terminals API 570 piping?
faq.a: It depends on who regulates them and how the owner has drawn its boundaries. Facility piping inside a refinery or terminal programme is normally inspected to API 570, while hazardous liquid pipelines and their facilities fall under PHMSA's 49 CFR Part 195 and the operator's integrity programme. The operator's documents set the split, and it can run through a single manifold. For the exam, apply API 570 to the piping the question tells you it covers.

faq.q: Which editions of API 570 and B31.3 are on the exam?
faq.a: For the February 2027 and June 2027 windows, the effectivity sheet lists the fifth edition of API 570 (February 2024), the 2024 edition of ASME B31.3, the 2020 edition of B16.5, the 2022 edition of PCC-2 for named articles, and the 2023 edition of ASME Sections V and IX. Later windows can move to newer editions, so always check the sheet for your window before you buy or download the documents.

faq.q: Which ASME Section V articles does the API 570 exam use?
faq.a: For the 2027 windows named above, the effectivity sheet lists Articles 1, 2, 6, 7, 9, 10 and 23, with Article 23 limited to SE-797, the ultrasonic thickness measurement practice. Articles 9 and 10 cover visual examination and leak testing, which the API 510 list does not include, so candidates who have already passed API 510 should not assume they know the 570 Section V scope.

faq.q: I take UT thickness readings for a contractor around Wood River. Does that count as experience?
faq.a: It can. API looks for supervision or performance of inspection activities as API 570 describes them, done while employed by or under contract to an authorized inspection agency, within the last ten years. CML readings taken as part of an owner's piping inspection programme fit that description better than isolated readings with no programme behind them. Keep records of the circuits, dates and your role, because API verifies the application.

faq.q: Should a St. Louis piping inspector add API 510 later?
faq.a: Many do, because refinery owner-users want inspectors who can move between vessels and piping during a turnaround. The two exams share RP 571, 576, 577 and 578, PCC-2 and ASME Sections V and IX, so the second one is shorter work than the first, but the mechanism lists and code calculations differ. A current API 570 certificate also qualifies you automatically to apply for API 580, which suits people moving towards inspection planning.

faq.q: Can a terminal operator enrol several technicians for API 570 prep?
faq.a: Yes. List the number of candidates, their current roles and the windows they are aiming for in one enquiry, and the quote covers the group. Each technician studies separately and sends their own questions to the instructor. Because API checks every application individually, it helps to collect each person's experience records early, particularly for technicians whose inspection time was spent with more than one contractor.
